title: AppLovin: cheap at about 14x FY27 EPS but conviction is low. The model says no position; a 1-share post-print starter would be an exception to the conviction rule.
call_reason: Conviction is below medium: the supervisor rated it low, so the allocator sized it at 0 shares (binding: conviction_below_min). The target of $292.84 is above the $268.22 price, so the target is not what blocks the trade; low conviction is.
one_liner: APP trades at about 14x FY27 EPS with a 6% FCF yield, $0.46B net debt and $1.8B of buyback left. Our $292.84 target (+9%) and $322 research target (12m) (+20%) are well below the Street's $512 median, and the model takes no position because conviction is low. The only trade on the table is a proposal awaiting your yes: 1 share (about $268) after the Q3 print and Q4 guide, expected around Wed Nov 4 but not yet announced. It is an explicit exception to the medium-conviction rule, justified by its effect on the book's Sharpe, not by a stronger view on the stock.

thesis.point: The business is still growing fast and is very profitable. The de-rating comes from slower growth, not shrinking earnings.
thesis.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $1,924M (+53% y/y), adjusted EBITDA $1,614M (84% margin), diluted EPS $3.76 and free cash flow $863.3M. The Q3 2026 guide is revenue of $2,055-2,085M (about +7.6% q/q at the midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $1,710-1,740M (83% margin).

thesis.point: Valuation and the balance sheet give a floor. Further downside needs earnings estimates to fall, not just the multiple.
thesis.evidence: At $268 the stock is about 14x FY27 consensus EPS of $20.00 and about a 6% FCF yield (supervisor). At Jun 30 2026: cash $3,053M against long-term debt $3,515M, so net debt is about $0.46B. Shares outstanding were 335.3M. The company bought back 3.28M shares for $1.5B in H1 2026, and $1.8B of authorization remains. The thesis break of $185 equals about 9x FY27 EPS and a 10%+ FCF yield.

thesis.point: The upside needs the estimate cuts to stop, and the Q4 guide is the first chance for that. This is why we would enter after the print, not before.
thesis.evidence: FY27 consensus EPS fell from $21.16 to $20.00 in 60 days (19 cuts, 5 raises; vendor data). Edgewater expects Q4 at +8-9% q/q (about $2.25B), against a consensus of about $2.27-2.28B. Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted pixel data (about 85% of new sites show no traffic) suggests e-commerce is a 2027 story. A Q4 guide at or above consensus would stop the cuts. A guide below about $2.25B would extend them.

variant_view: Our variant view is against the sell side, not against the options market. Our blended 12-month target is $292.84 (P(gain) 0.55). The 24 analysts' weighted mean is $511 (median $512, range $325-790, rating Buy). We think those targets are stale: they assume a re-rating that falling revisions do not support. In the last two months BofA moved to $400 and Piper to $325, and Wells Fargo is at $325. The options market alone implies $252 (P(gain) 0.46). We sit modestly above it because valuation support (14x, 6% FCF yield, buybacks) has not yet broken. That edge over the options market is small, about +$41 in the median, and at about 68% implied vol it is not a strong variant view. The supervisor said plainly that no verified fact shows a clear edge per unit of risk. [sources 20, 23, 24, 25, 18, 22]

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $322, against the agents' range of $310-348 (mean $326). Three methods, blended: (1) P/E: FY27 EPS of about $19.2 (consensus $20.00 less about 4%), rolled to an NTM EPS of about $22 at Oct 2027, at about 15x = about $330. (2) FCF yield: FY27E FCF of about $6.4B / about 328M shares at a 6-6.3% yield = about $310-325. (3) EV/EBITDA: 11-12x on about $8.1B, less $0.46B net debt = about $290-320. Share base: 335.3M at Jun 30 2026 (10-Q), falling to about 326-330M with buybacks. The 12-month target ($292.84) is the calibrated median of a 67% options-market / 33% agent blend. Scenario range across agents: bear $170-190 (22-30%), base $310-325 (45-53%), bull $475-500 (25-27%). Model take-profit $453.69 (q75); stop $180.70 (2x 1M IV noise floor). [sources 2, 20, 22]

catalysts.event: AppLovin announces the date of its Q3 2026 report
catalysts.why_it_moves: It only sets the timing. It decides when the 1-share entry window opens.
catalysts.watch: A 'to Announce Third Quarter 2026 Results' release on the IR feed or Business Wire. None was out as of Oct 3; the Q1 and Q2 date notices came out Apr 1 and Jul 1.

catalysts.event: Ruling on AppLovin's TRO application against Unity's Ad Quality SDK (SF Superior Court), and the JAMS arbitration (filing reported by trade press; not verified from a court record)
catalysts.why_it_moves: It tests whether MAX auction data, the core of the gaming moat, is leaking to the fastest-growing competitor.
catalysts.watch: Whether the TRO is granted or denied, and what Unity says about the SDK's data collection.

catalysts.why_it_moves: High-beta, high-multiple ad-tech is rate-sensitive. A surprise hike would hit it harder than the book.
catalysts.watch: Hold versus hike, and the press-conference tone.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Read-through on mobile ad demand and on competitors' AI ad and game tools (Google AdMob is a direct mediation competitor).
catalysts.watch: Commentary on Audience Network and AdMob, and on Meta's AI game-creation tools.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Unity guided Strategic Grow to $380-385M (+68-70% y/y, about +16% q/q). A beat says Vector is taking spread or share from AppLovin.
catalysts.watch: Strategic Grow against $385M, the Q4 Grow guide, and any comment on the AppLovin dispute.

catalysts.date: around 2026-11-04 (Wed; company has not announced it)
catalysts.event: AppLovin Q3 2026 results and Q4 guide. This is the proposed entry point for the 1 share.
catalysts.why_it_moves: It is the first print since the Q2 miss. The Q4 guide decides whether FY27 estimate cuts stop. Q2 moved the stock about 16-21% in a day.
catalysts.watch: Q3 revenue against the $2,055-2,085M guide and adjusted EBITDA against $1,710-1,740M. Above all, the Q4 guide against Edgewater's about $2.25B and consensus of about $2.27-2.28B. Also e-commerce and self-serve commentary, buyback pace (Q2 was $551M), and the 10-Q litigation note. The date pattern: Q3 2025 was reported Wed Nov 5 2025, and Q1 and Q2 2026 on Wednesdays May 6 and Aug 5.

catalysts.event: Lead-plaintiff deadline in Talbot v. AppLovin (N.D. Cal. 3:26-cv-10584, filed Sep 16 2026; class period Feb 12 - Aug 5 2026)
catalysts.why_it_moves: It starts the amended-complaint and motion-to-dismiss cycle. The CEO's discretionary sales inside the class period give plaintiffs scienter material. The deadline date comes from the statutory PSLRA notice.
catalysts.watch: Appointment of the lead plaintiff, then the amended complaint.

catalysts.event: Ruling on the motion to dismiss in the 2025 securities class action (fully briefed as of Feb 2026, per the 10-Q)
catalysts.why_it_moves: A denial would extend the legal overhang and the governance discount. A dismissal would remove one of the two cases.
catalysts.watch: The N.D. Cal. docket. The derivative suits are stayed pending this ruling.

catalysts.event: Holiday-season sell-side alt-data on e-commerce (Wells Fargo traffic-weighted pixel data, Citi/Store Leads merchant counts)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Notes like these have moved the stock 3-5% in a day, and e-commerce is the bull case's growth leg.
catalysts.watch: Whether the share of new pixel sites with traffic rises from about 15%.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Rate path for long-duration growth stocks.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results and first 2027 commentary (Q4 2025 was reported Feb 11 2026). This is the add-or-exit checkpoint.
catalysts.why_it_moves: It shows whether the Q4 guide held and how big e-commerce was in the holiday quarter.
catalysts.watch: Q4 against its guide, the Q1 2027 guide, and whether FY27 consensus EPS stabilises at about $20 or above.

risks.risk: Gaming share and spread loss to Unity Vector. Unity is growing about 16% q/q against AppLovin's about 7.6% (in dollars about $53M against $146M a quarter).
risks.signpost: Unity Q3 Strategic Grow at or above $385M with another mid-teens q/q guide, while AppLovin's Q4 guide comes in below +8% q/q, or AppLovin loses the TRO.

risks.risk: The Q4 guide misses and estimate cuts continue. The 14x multiple is only cheap if FY27 EPS of about $20 holds.
risks.signpost: A Q4 revenue guide midpoint below about $2.25B, and FY27 consensus EPS below $19 within two weeks of the print.

risks.risk: E-commerce and self-serve stays a false start, which removes the bull case's growth leg for 2027.
risks.signpost: No improvement through the holidays in the share of traffic-weighted pixel sites with traffic, and management declining to size the e-commerce contribution on the Q3 or Q4 call.

risks.risk: Litigation and governance. There are two securities class actions (2025 and Talbot 2026). The CEO sold about $51.1M in June 2026 (104,166 shares at $473.55-516.51) and about $46.2M in March 2026, all on Form 4s marked not under a Rule 10b5-1 plan, inside the Talbot class period.
risks.signpost: The motion to dismiss is denied in the 2025 case, the Talbot amended complaint leans on the insider sales, or any new regulator inquiry is disclosed in the Q3 10-Q.

trade.position: Proposed: 1 sh (about $268 at the $268.22 close, about 2.7% of the $9,976 book). This is an explicit EXCEPTION to the medium-conviction rule. The model allocation is 0 shares because the supervisor rated conviction low (binding: conviction_below_min). The case for the exception is the portfolio effect: 1 APP share, alongside 1 AMZN share, raises the book's Sharpe on invested money from about 0.60 to about 0.68. 1 share is slightly above the supervisor's 2.5% cap (about $249), and a single share cannot be split into the supervisor's two tranches.
trade.entry: Do not buy before the print. Buy 1 share after the Q3 2026 report and Q4 guide (expected around Wed Nov 4 2026; the company has not announced the date as of Oct 3), and only if all three hold: (a) the Q4 revenue guide midpoint is at or above about $2.25B (Edgewater's bar); (b) the stock is above the $185 thesis break; (c) nothing new turns up in litigation or the Unity dispute. This adapts the supervisor's two-tranche plan (half after Q3, half after Q4 in Feb 2027) to a 1-share size. If the guide misses, there is no trade.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit if: the stock closes below the $180.70 stop or holds below the $185 thesis break (loss at stop about $88, about 0.9% of the book); the Q4 2026 report (around mid-Feb 2027) misses its own guide, or the Q1 2027 guide implies flat or negative q/q; FY27 consensus EPS falls below about $18; or AppLovin loses the Unity dispute in a way that exposes MAX auction data. Take profit at $453.69. Add a 2nd share only after the Q4 2026 report, if the guide held, FY27 revisions have stopped falling, and the supervisor's conviction rating rises to medium. Until then the position stays at 1 share as an exception.

what_changes_our_mind: Bullish: a Q4 guide at or above about $2.28B, with management quantifying e-commerce, and FY27 consensus EPS turning up from $20.00. This would justify medium conviction and a normal-sized position.
Bearish: a Q4 guide implying less than about +5% q/q, or a sustained trade below $185. Either would mean the market expects earnings to fall; we would drop the idea and not buy the exception share.

Competitive: Unity Q3 Strategic Grow beats $385M and guides Q4 to another mid-teens q/q while AppLovin decelerates, or the TRO is denied and Unity keeps collecting MAX auction data. Either would move weight to the bear case ($170-190).
